item.title: China Buys More US Soybeans as Key Agricultural Trade Ramps Up
item.description: China has purchased more soybeans from the US, according to people familiar with the matter, as the key agricultural trade gains momentum following a summit between the leaders of the two nations in May.

item.title: India Property Developer K Raheja Said to Delay $700 Million IPO
item.description: K Raheja Corp. Pvt., one of India’s largest real estate developers, has delayed plans for an initial public offering after feedback from investment bankers, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Europe’s Defense Stocks Rally Has Much Riding on NATO Summit
item.description: A fledgling rebound in European defense stocks faces a test this week, as investors look to a NATO summit for further clarity on member states’ defense spending plans.

item.title: Mystery Thai Investor’s Near $1 Billion True Stake Sparks Probe
item.description: Thailand’s market regulator is probing the sudden emergence of an individual shareholder who has amassed nearly $1 billion worth of shares in True Corp., making her one of the telecom giant’s largest shareholders.

item.title: A Token Grasp of the AI Boom Shows Trouble Brewing
item.description: The period of vertical ascent is probably over.

item.title: Japan’s Inpex Signs 15-Year Deal to Buy Persian Gulf LNG
item.description: Japan’s state-backed Inpex Corp. signed a 15-year deal with Abu Dhabi National Oil Co. for the supply of liquefied natural gas from its project in the Persian Gulf.

item.title: Japan 30-Year Bonds Rise After Strong Demand Reassures Investors
item.description: Japan’s 30-year government bonds rose after an auction of the tenor drew its strongest demand since 2019, as high yield levels attracted investors despite worries about fiscal policy and inflation.

item.title: PBOC Unveils New Measures to Cement Hong Kong’s Yuan Hub Status
item.description: China’s central bank announced a slew of measures aimed at expanding an investment channel between Hong Kong’s financial market and the mainland, as well as enhancing the city’s role in promoting overseas use of the yuan.

item.title: India’s Unloved Heavyweight Stocks May Be Poised for a Rebound
item.description: A combination of under-ownership and attractive valuations could draw buyers.

item.title: Samsung Results Trigger Stock Rotation to Less Loved Sectors
item.description: Asian tech stocks slumped, as investors used Samsung Electronics Co.’s results to lock in profits on a stellar year-to-date chip rally, rotating into unloved sectors less prone to earnings shocks.

item.title: Chinese Firms Leave Nvidia for Local AI Suppliers, Survey Shows
item.description: Chinese companies are ditching Nvidia Corp.’s advanced accelerators in favor of domestic silicon, underscoring how tensions with the US are reshaping the AI infrastructure buildout and propelling Beijing’s ambitions to substitute American technology.

item.title: Japan Isn’t Pushing for Low Interest Rates, Growth Minister Says
item.description: Media reports that claim Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s administration is attempting to keep interest rates low and weaken fiscal improvement efforts aren’t accurate at all, according to Japan’s Growth Strategy Minister Minoru Kiuchi.

item.title: Hong Kong Begins Trial Operation of New Gold Clearing System
item.description: Hong Kong has launched the trial operation of a new gold clearing system, backed by several major banks, in a key step toward its ambition to become a significant bullion-trading hub with price-setting power.

item.title: Philippines Says Inflation Pressure Still Strong After June Data
item.description: Philippine inflation eased for a second month, but the central bank said consumer price pressures remain strong and is prepared to take further monetary action to ensure that it returns to target.

item.title: Wall Street Warms to India’s Markets as Oil Pressures Fade
item.description: After spending more than a year on the sidelines, global investors are showing fresh interest in India as sentiment begins to improve across the country’s markets.

item.title: Hanwha Ocean Plunges Over 20% After Losing Canada Sub Deal
item.description: Shares of Hanwha Ocean fell more than 23% on Tuesday morning after Canada picked a German bid to replace its aging submarine fleet over the South Korean shipbuilder’s proposal.

item.title: Island Pharma Jumps After Emergency-Use Approval for Ebola Drug
item.description: Australia’s Island Pharmaceuticals Ltd. surged as much as 47% after saying its experimental antiviral galidesivir had secured regulatory and ethics approvals for emergency use in patients with the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola in Uganda.

item.title: WiseTech Shares Jump After Billionaire White Quits as Chair
item.description: Billionaire Richard White has stepped down as chair of WiseTech Global Ltd., just weeks after denying he was involved in human trafficking amid reports he was being investigated by police over claims he used a woman’s immigration status for sex.

item.title: Myanmar Bets on Ancient Temples, Buddhist Pilgrimage Sites to Boost Tourism
item.description: Myanmar’s ancient temples, luxury hotels and Buddhist pilgrimage sites are stirring back to life as the country’s military-backed government bets tourism will become one of the first visible signs of an economic recovery after this year’s election.

item.title: LG Energy Profit Misses Estimates Amid Slow EV Demand
item.description: LG Energy Solution Ltd. reported preliminary second-quarter earnings that missed analyst estimates, as lackluster support for electric vehicles in key markets like the US failed to offset surging demand for energy storage systems.

item.title: Japan’s Nominal Wages Top 3% Again in Longest Streak Since 1992
item.description: Japanese wages climbed again in May, comfortably outpacing inflation and reinforcing the Bank of Japan’s stance toward raising interest rates.

item.title: Gold Steadies as Traders Look to Fed for Interest-Rate Outlook
item.description: Gold was little changed as traders awaited minutes from the Federal Reserve’s last meeting for fresh insights into the path for US interest rates.

item.title: JPMorgan Asset Bets Strong Yuan, Weak Won Trend Will Flip
item.description: JPMorgan Asset Management has trimmed its long yuan positions against the dollar, shifting its focus to higher yielding currencies, as the yuan’s outperformance begins to cool.

item.title: Samsung Profit Surges Past Estimates on AI Memory Chip Demand
item.description: Samsung Electronics Co.’s quarterly profit surged 19-fold, just surpassing elevated expectations due to relentless demand for memory chips needed in AI data centers.

item.title: Intel-Backed AI Chip and Software Maker Syntiant Files for IPO
item.description: Syntiant Corp., a company making semiconductors and software for artificial intelligence, filed for an initial public offering to tap investors’ enthusiasm for the technology.

item.title: Peru’s Central Bank Chief Agrees to Extend 20-Year Run
item.description: Peru’s central bank chief Julio Velarde, seen as a pillar of economic stability in the politically volatile Andean nation, has agreed to stay on for another term, likely extending one of the world’s longest tenures at the helm of a monetary authority.

item.title: Asian Stocks to Gain, Samsung Slides After Profit: Markets Wrap
item.description: Stocks in Asia are poised to edge higher after a rally in several US technology giants revived confidence that the AI-driven bull market still has room to run.

item.title: Oil Holds Drop as Saudi Arabian Price Cut Amplifies Glut Concern
item.description: Oil held a drop on signs of growing global oversupply, with Saudi Arabia slashing prices of its main grade to Asia and maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz picking up.

item.title: Japan Drives Asia Offshore Bonds to Record, Surpassing China Era
item.description: Japanese borrowers drove quarterly issuance in Asia Pacific’s offshore bond market to a record, eclipsing the previous peak set during an era of Chinese corporate dominance.

item.title: Rivian Offers 75 Million Shares to Meet US Energy Loan Terms
item.description: Rivian Automotive Inc. is offering to sell 75 million shares as the electric vehicle company seeks to fund equity contributions related to a US Department of Energy loan.
